brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
Mizoram tea is an orthodox black tea from the hills of the northeastern Indian state of Mizoram. It is said to take a smoky character from bamboo baskets hung over a fire.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: Accounts describe traditional bamboo baskets used during withering, and sellers offer orthodox and summer black teas under the name. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Orthodox processing; leaves are reportedly placed in bamboo baskets hung over a fire during withering.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Usually dark twisted leaf, sometimes with golden tips.
taste_profile: Described as strong, bold, smoky and earthy, with a slightly sweet aftertaste.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
